item.title: Sherrod Brown Tries a New Retort to Criticism on Transgender Issues
item.description: A spot from the Senate candidate in Ohio seeks to dismiss the Republican Party’s focus on transgender rights as a distraction from economic issues.

item.title: Trump Won Their Votes. Now His Trade War Is Dividing Them.

item.dc:creator: Tim Balk, Oralandar Brand-Williams and Jesse Ellison
item.media:description: Flags of Canada and United States fly across the international border on the Gordie Howe International bridge, which links Windsor, Ontario, with Detroit.

item.title: Texas Billionaire John Poindexter Plans to Revive Shafter Ghost Town
item.description: An 81-year-old billionaire has a vision for preserving a tiny West Texas mining town, even as other forces are reshaping the land around it.
item.dc:creator: Sasha von Oldershausen and Christopher Lee
item.media:description: “This has always been a cross-border community,” said John Poindexter, owner of the West Texas luxury hotel Cibolo Creek Ranch.

item.title: Kennedy Center Supporters Rally Amid Fears of Trump’s Demolition

item.media:description: Demonstrators denounced the vote by the center’s board to close one of the nation’s premier performing arts venues.

item.title: Russia Aims to Inject Chaos Into Elections, U.S. Intelligence Finds
item.description: The Kremlin is once again seeking to undermine confidence in American democracy with online influence campaigns, U.S. officials said.
item.dc:creator: Dustin Volz, Julian E. Barnes and Steven Lee Myers
item.category: Office of the Director of National Intelligence
item.media:credit: Sean Rayford for The New York Times
item.media:description: Since 2016, Russia has tried to influence every federal election cycle, according to previously declassified assessments.

item.title: F.A.A. to Roll Out New A.I. Tool for Washington Airports
item.description: The tool, called SMART, will crunch scheduling and weather data to predict and avoid delays. It will be deployed in the Washington region’s three major airports next week.
item.dc:creator: Aishvarya Kavi and Karoun Demirjian
item.media:credit: Kent Nishimura for The New York Times
item.media:description: SMART, a new A.I. air traffic control tool, will soon be deployed in Ronald Reagan Washington National Airport. Officials say it will not replace human air traffic controllers.

item.title: F.A.A. Safety Request for the Top of Trump’s Arch: Eternal Fire
item.description: The aviation agency deemed the mammoth arch safe for air travel if it includes a constant flame and other safety measures to help make it visible to planes.
item.dc:creator: Luke Broadwater
item.media:description: President Trump plans for the arch to be 250 feet tall, dwarfing even the Arc de Triomphe in Paris.

item.title: St. Paul Mayor’s Behavior Faulted After Police Chief’s Complaint
item.description: An outside investigation found that Mayor Kaohly Her had engaged in offensive behavior, but found no evidence that she sexually harassed colleagues. It did find that she had engaged in “offensive” behavior.
item.dc:creator: Ernesto Londoño
item.media:credit: Jenn Ackerman for The New York Times
item.media:description: Mayor Kaohly Her of St. Paul was accused of behaving inappropriately toward city employees.

item.title: Cost of Iran War Estimated at $43.6 Billion
item.description: For the first time, the Pentagon reported costs incurred by each armed service. The figures are almost certainly on the low side, congressional officials said.

item.category: United States Defense and Military Forces
US and Israeli Attack on Iran (2026)
item.media:credit: Arash Khamooshi/Polaris for The New York Times
item.media:description: An apartment building that was targeted by U.S.-Israeli airstrikes in Tehran in March. The unclassified Pentagon cost estimates provided to Congress offer a rare glimpse into the financial accounting of the war.

item.title: Judge Who Struck Down Trump’s Compensation Fund Asks: Will Trump Just Pay Allies Another Way?

item.dc:creator: Alan Feuer

item.title: Trump Courts North Korea’s Leader, but Might Need China to Reignite the Flame
item.description: President Trump has gotten no love back yet from Kim Jong-un. He could turn to Xi Jinping, China’s leader, to help set up a summit when Mr. Xi visits Washington next week.
item.dc:creator: Edward Wong
item.media:description: President Trump and Kim Jong-un on the North Korean side of the Demilitarized Zone in 2019. For Mr. Trump, a summit with Mr. Kim would help him turn the spotlight away from the unpopular war against Iran and toward a leader-to-leader relationship that Mr. Trump has treasured since his first term.

item.title: James Talarico, Seeking Black Votes in Texas Senate Rate, Wins Crucial Endorsement
item.description: The Congressional Black Caucus’s political wing backed James Talarico, who defeated a Black opponent in the primary. He faces Ken Paxton, the Republican state attorney general, in November.
item.dc:creator: Neil Vigdor
item.media:description: James Talarico has pledged that his campaign would spend $25 million on outreach to Black voters.

item.title: Trump Calls A.I. Fears a Hoax. Inside the White House, the Debate Is More Complex.

item.dc:creator: David E. Sanger, Jonathan Swan, Cecilia Kang and Dustin Volz
item.media:description: President Trump at a dinner with David Sacks and Mark Zuckerberg at the White House last year.

item.title: How Trump Became an A.I. Evangelist
item.description: President Trump had little interest in artificial intelligence until a fateful meeting in Las Vegas two years ago. Now, Mr. Trump sees A.I. as the defining technology of our age. Our White House correspondent Jonathan Swan tracks Trump’s journey to A.I. evangelist.
item.dc:creator: Jonathan Swan, John Pappas, Chris Whitworth, Brian Oh, Nikolay Nikolov and Whitney Shefte

item.title: F.B.I. Temporarily Halted Cooperation With Canada Over References to 9/11
item.description: The abrupt move by Kash Patel, the bureau’s director, came as President Trump was ramping up his attacks on the country.
item.dc:creator: Maggie Haberman, Jane Bradley, Jonathan Swan, Adam Goldman and Matina Stevis-Gridneff
item.media:description: The abrupt move by Kash Patel risked jeopardizing the F.B.I.’s relationship with Canada’s national law enforcement agency, which works closely with the bureau on a wide range of issues, including terrorism and cybersecurity cases.

item.title: Trump’s Open Claims That He Directs Super PAC Spending Draw Watchdog Complaint
item.description: Federal law bars those holding federal office from directing spending decisions for a political organization with no contribution limits.
item.dc:creator: Shane Goldmacher and Maggie Haberman
item.media:description: President Trump has repeatedly proclaimed that he controls spending of MAGA Inc., the super PAC his advisers run. A new complaint argues this is against the law.
